## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Jentātherīgāthā* (Thig 2.2) is a short poetic text preserved in the *Therīgāthā* section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The verses are attributed to the elder nun (*therī*) Jentā, who is identified in historical studies as one of several prominent Licchavi women who renounced household life to enter the Buddhist monastic order (*bhikkhuṇī-saṅgha*) [Hazra 1995]. Modern English translations of the text have been prepared by Ayya Soma and Bhikkhu Sujato, with thirteen translations available across ten languages [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral records no curated cross-canonical parallels for this poem [SuttaCentral]. Algorithmic text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus detects fifteen Pali-internal matches across two commentary texts, displaying extensive reuse in the commentary to the collection, the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (segments §0.3–2.4 aligning with §335–339), and sharing phrasing with the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (segments §2.3–2.4 aligning with §1738_2–1738_3) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language alignments with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections met the similarity threshold (score ≥ 10) [DharmaNexus].
